answer: Grading work is drawn each epoch by a lottery seeded with a secret published only after the epoch closes. A text goes to graders it has never touched, and any identity holding more than a few assignments is trimmed to a cap, the surplus returned to the pool. A farm can mint a thousand accounts, yet the draw hands them almost none, and since the seed is hidden until close, staking early buys no advantage. One real slot means staying present and unremarkable across many quiet epochs. On a still lagoon the echo of a single raven sounds like a flock; here the count holds.
